subject: math.IT
name: Kraft–McMillan inequality
statement: For a uniquely decodable code over an alphabet of size r ≥ 2 with finite codeword lengths l₁, …, lₘ, the lengths satisfy Σᵢ r^(−lᵢ) ≤ 1. Conversely, every finite list of nonnegative integer lengths satisfying this inequality is realized by a prefix code, with the length-zero case permitted only when there is one source symbol.

subject: math.IT
name: Shannon source coding theorem
statement: Let X₁, X₂, … be independent identically distributed random variables on a finite alphabet with entropy H(X), measured in bits. Let Lₙ be the minimum expected length of a binary prefix code for the positive-probability sequences (X₁, …, Xₙ), allowing the empty codeword when there is only one such sequence. Then nH(X) ≤ Lₙ < nH(X) + 1, so the optimal expected number of bits per source symbol converges to H(X).

subject: math.IT
name: Shannon noisy-channel coding theorem
statement: For a discrete memoryless channel with finite input and output alphabets, its capacity in bits per use is C = maxₚ₍ₓ₎ I(X; Y). Every rate 0 ≤ R < C is achievable by a sequence of block codes whose decoding error probability tends to zero, while no sequence with asymptotic rate strictly greater than C can have error probability tending to zero.

subject: math.IT
name: Strong converse for discrete memoryless channels
statement: Consider block codes of length n for a fixed discrete memoryless channel with finite alphabets and capacity C, with messages chosen uniformly. If liminfₙ (log₂ Mₙ)/n > C, where Mₙ is the number of messages, then the average decoding error probability tends to one.

subject: math.IT
name: Shannon–Hartley theorem
statement: An ideal band-limited additive white Gaussian noise channel of bandwidth B hertz, average signal power P, and total noise power N within that bandwidth has capacity C = B log₂(1 + P/N) bits per second. The formula assumes B > 0, N > 0, and an average-power constraint.

subject: math.IT
name: Data processing inequality
statement: If finite-valued random variables X, Y, Z form a Markov chain X → Y → Z, meaning X and Z are conditionally independent given Y, then I(X; Z) ≤ I(X; Y). Thus processing Y through a channel cannot increase its mutual information with X.

subject: math.IT
name: Gibbs' inequality
statement: For probability distributions p and q on a finite set, the relative entropy D(p ∥ q) = Σₓ p(x) log₂(p(x)/q(x)) is nonnegative and equals zero exactly when p = q. Terms with p(x) = 0 are zero, and D(p ∥ q) is infinite if p(x) > 0 but q(x) = 0 for some x.

subject: math.IT
name: Fano's inequality
statement: Let X take values in an alphabet of size m ≥ 2, and let X̂ be an estimate determined by an observation Y and taking values in that same alphabet. If Pₑ = Pr(X̂ ≠ X), then H(X | Y) ≤ h₂(Pₑ) + Pₑ log₂(m − 1), where h₂ is binary entropy and all entropies are in bits.

subject: math.IT
name: Asymptotic equipartition property
statement: If X₁, X₂, … are independent identically distributed random variables on a finite alphabet, then −(1/n) log₂ Pr(X₁, …, Xₙ) converges almost surely to H(X₁), where the probability is evaluated at the realized sequence. Consequently, long typical source sequences have probabilities exponentially close to 2^(−nH(X₁)).

subject: math.IT
name: Slepian–Wolf theorem
statement: For independent identically distributed pairs (Xᵢ, Yᵢ) on finite alphabets, X and Y can be encoded separately and reconstructed jointly with block error probability tending to zero. The closure of the achievable rate region, in bits per pair, is exactly Rₓ ≥ H(X | Y), Rᵧ ≥ H(Y | X), and Rₓ + Rᵧ ≥ H(X, Y).

subject: math.IT
name: Shannon rate-distortion theorem
statement: For an independent identically distributed source X on a finite alphabet, a finite reproduction alphabet, a bounded single-letter distortion d, and a feasible distortion level D, the minimum asymptotic coding rate under expected distortion at most D is R(D) = min I(X; X̂). The minimum ranges over conditional distributions of X̂ given X satisfying E[d(X, X̂)] ≤ D; rates strictly above R(D) are achievable with asymptotic distortion at most D.

subject: math.IT
name: Huffman coding optimality theorem
statement: For a finite source alphabet with assigned symbol probabilities, Huffman’s algorithm constructs a binary prefix code minimizing the expected codeword length among all binary prefix codes for that alphabet. The construction repeatedly merges the two least probable remaining symbols or subtrees.

subject: math.IT
name: Hamming bound
statement: Let q ≥ 2 and let t be an integer with 0 ≤ t ≤ n. If a q-ary code of length n contains M codewords and has minimum Hamming distance at least 2t + 1, then M Σⱼ₌₀ᵗ binomial(n, j)(q − 1)^j ≤ qⁿ, because its radius-t Hamming balls are disjoint.

subject: math.IT
name: Singleton bound
statement: For q ≥ 2, a q-ary code of length n containing M ≥ 2 codewords and having minimum Hamming distance 1 ≤ d ≤ n satisfies M ≤ q^(n − d + 1). In particular, a nonzero linear [n, k, d] code over the finite field with q elements satisfies k ≤ n − d + 1.

subject: math.IT
name: Gilbert–Varshamov bound
statement: For integers q ≥ 2 and 1 ≤ d ≤ n, there exists a q-ary code of length n and minimum Hamming distance at least d containing at least qⁿ / Σⱼ₌₀^(d−1) binomial(n, j)(q − 1)^j codewords. A maximal code under inclusion has this bound because its radius-(d − 1) Hamming balls cover all qⁿ words.

subject: math.IT
name: Reed–Solomon minimum-distance theorem
statement: Let q be a prime power and let 1 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ q. Evaluating every polynomial of degree less than k over the field with q elements at n distinct field elements gives a linear [n, k, n − k + 1] code, attaining the Singleton bound.

subject: math.IT
name: Plotkin bound
statement: For a q-ary code of length n, size M, and minimum Hamming distance d with qd > (q − 1)n, the size satisfies M ≤ floor(qd / (qd − (q − 1)n)). The bound follows by comparing the sum of all pairwise distances with the maximum possible contribution of each coordinate.

subject: math.IT
name: Entropy power inequality
statement: Let X and Y be independent random vectors in ℝⁿ with densities, finite differential entropies, and finite second moments. Defining entropy power by N(X) = (1/(2πe)) exp(2h(X)/n), with h measured in nats, gives N(X + Y) ≥ N(X) + N(Y).

subject: math.IT
name: Nyquist–Shannon sampling theorem
statement: Let f be a square-integrable signal whose Fourier transform, using frequency in hertz, vanishes outside [−B, B], where B > 0. Its continuous representative is determined by the samples f(k/(2B)) and is reconstructed by f(t) = Σₖ∈ℤ f(k/(2B)) sinc(2Bt − k), with convergence in the square-integrable norm and sinc(u) = sin(πu)/(πu).

subject: math.IT
name: Shannon perfect-secrecy key-entropy bound
statement: Suppose finite-valued message M and key K are independent, a ciphertext C is produced by encryption, and M is recovered exactly from (C, K). If the system has perfect secrecy, meaning M and C are independent, then H(K) ≥ H(M).
